# SetCameraStencil <img class="product" src="media/bl-20x14.png" alt="BlitzLLVM" title="BlitzLLVM" width="20" height="14">

<div align="center">

[Command Index](Command-Index) · [Blitz3D](Blitz3D) · [Cameras](Blitz3D-Cameras)

</div>


```blitzbasic
SetCameraStencil:Void camera:Int32, enabled:Int32
```

| Parameter | Mode | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `camera` | In | Int32 | required | Camera handle. |
| `enabled` | In | Int32 | required | True for a stencil, False for none (the default). |

## Description

<img class="product" src="media/bl-20x14.png" alt="BlitzLLVM" title="BlitzLLVM" width="20" height="14"> This command does not exist in the original Blitz products. BlitzLLVM adds it.

Gives a camera a stencil buffer: 8 bits for every pixel, next to the depth buffer, which entities with [SetEntityStencil](SetEntityStencil) test and change while the camera draws. A stencil can mask out a part of the picture (a portal, a window into another scene, the inside of a mirror), count overlaps, or build shadow volumes. Without this, the camera has no stencil and entities draw as if they had none. This is a BlitzLLVM extension.

The camera clears the stencil of its viewport to 0 when it starts drawing; [SetCameraStencilClear](SetCameraStencilClear) changes that. Cameras that draw to targets of the same size share one depth buffer, so they also share the stencil: a second camera that clears neither depth nor stencil sees what the first one left.

A stencil costs one byte per pixel and a slightly slower depth buffer, so it is only there for cameras that ask for it. Entities that use order-independent transparency (`BLITZLLVM_OIT` 1 to 5) and 2D drawing ignore the stencil.

## Examples

```blitzbasic
Graphics3D 640, 480, 0, 2
SetBuffer BackBuffer()
camera = CreateCamera()
SetCameraStencil camera, True

; The window: drawn first (EntityOrder 1), it sets the stencil to 1 where it is.
window = CreateCube()
EntityOrder window, 1
PositionEntity window, 0, 0, 10
SetEntityStencil window, 7, 1, 255, 255, 0, 0, 2

; The world behind it is only drawn where the stencil is 1.
sphere = CreateSphere(32)
EntityColor sphere, 255, 128, 0
PositionEntity sphere, 0, 0, 20
ScaleEntity sphere, 8, 8, 8
SetEntityStencil sphere, 2, 1

RenderWorld
Flip
WaitKey
```
